q: A pipeline has run for months. In a code clean-up, the flow `web_flow` that appends into `orders_all` is renamed to `web_orders_flow`. What happens at the next update?
o: Nothing changes: the pipeline matches flows by their query
The pipeline refuses to start until you run a full refresh
The renamed flow starts with a new, empty checkpoint and appends the whole source again, creating duplicates
The old checkpoint is renamed together with the flow
e: The flow name is how the pipeline finds the checkpoint. A new name means no checkpoint, so the flow reads the source from the beginning and appends everything again.

q: What is the default (implicit) flow of `CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE t AS SELECT * FROM STREAM(src)`?
o: A flow named `t`, created with the table, that writes the query's rows into `t`
There is none: only `CREATE FLOW` creates flows
A flow named `src`
A one-time backfill flow
e: Defining a table with a query creates the table and its flow in one step, and the flow takes the table's name.

q: Three sources feed one streaming table through a single `UNION ALL` query. A fourth source must be added. Why is the multi-flow pattern better here?
o: A UNION query cannot read streaming sources
With one flow per source, only the new flow backfills; with the UNION, the changed query needs a full refresh of all sources
Multi-flow tables need no checkpoints
UNION queries cannot write to streaming tables
e: A UNION is one flow with one checkpoint. Changing it means starting over for every source. Separate flows keep separate checkpoints, so a new flow only reads its own source.

q: You want every row from every flow into `orders_all` to have a positive `quantity`, dropping the rest. Where do you write the rule?
o: In each `CREATE FLOW` statement
In a separate expectations file
In the pipeline settings
As `CONSTRAINT ... EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION DROP ROW` on the `orders_all` table definition
e: Expectations cannot be defined on a flow. They live on the target table and apply to all flows that write into it.

q: Old orders exist as CSV exports and must be loaded into `orders_all` one time, next to the flows that keep running. What fits?
o: Add the files to the UNION query of the table
A flow with `INSERT INTO ONCE` (or `@dp.append_flow(..., once=True)`)
Rename an existing flow so it re-reads everything
Set `pipelines.reset.allowed = false`
e: A ONCE flow is a backfill: it runs one time instead of on every update, and the regular flows are not affected.
